newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian parties in boycott over Kurd murders.
newsitem.headline: Austrian parties in boycott over Kurd murders.

text.p: Austrian opposition parties said on Thursday they would boycott parliamentary business in a bid to force a parliamentary investigation into the murder of three Kurdish activists in Vienna eight years ago.

The opposition Greens, Liberals and far-right Freedom Party announced at a joint press conference that they would block proceedings until June 10. They are demanding a parliamentary inquiry into the government's handling of the case and the flight of suspected Iranian assassins.
The opposition holds 60 of the 183 seats in the assembly which is dominated by the ruling coalition of Social Democrats and conservative People's Party.

"The opposition has already made four attempts to force the government to set up a parliamentary committee to look into the matter but each time thay have failed because of the government's majority," the three parties said in a statement.

Iranian Kurdish leader Abdorrahman Qasemlu and two other activists were slain by suspected Iranian hitmen in July 1989. Former Iranian president Abolhassan Bani-Sadr and Austrian diplomats have alleged that ministers bowed to pressure from Iran to let the suspects flee Austria.
Warrants for their arrest were not issued until they were outside the country.
